newsitem.title: USA: Dec S&P 500 futures seen eyeing 706.00 by Friday.
newsitem.headline: Dec S&P 500 futures seen eyeing 706.00 by Friday.

text.p: December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures are poised to easily hurdle the 700.00 level and climb toward 706.00, possibly before Friday's September U.S. employment report, technicians said.
Nearby S&P 500 futures early on Wednesday rose to a new all-time high for a lead-month contract, leaping past the old peak of 697.50 set on September 24.
The contract, buoyed by a continued strong performance in U.S. Treasury bond futures, touched 700.00 after midday on Wednesday.

Despite the contract's slightly overbought condition -- the relative strength index was above 70 heading into Wednesday's session -- analysts said other factors could prevail near-term, especially if S&P 500s and T-bond futures close strong.
"A close in this region, above this series of highs we've gotten to...above 697.50 would be great," said Steve Boyajian, director of technical analysis, MMS International.

If that occurs, Boyajian expected S&Ps could rise to a measuring objective at 711.25, derived from the rally shown on the daily bar chart from the July 16 low at 616.05 to the August 22 peak at 678.50 to the September 3 low at 648.80.
"I think we could could hit this target (711.25) by the end of the week," Boyajian added.

"I still basically feel from here that we'll be moving on up to about 706.00, probably within the next couple days," said Terence Gabriel, technical analyst, I.D.E.A. Inc. "And then further on from there, I think it's also reasonable to look for a move on up to 725.00 as medium-term target."

Gabriel cited several reasons for his bias, noting that the trends in most major equity indices "are strongly positive, so that I'm looking basically for the Dow to move on up to 6,000 in fairly near term and then up to 6,200."
Currently, each point in S&P 500 futures roughly equals 8.5 points in the Dow 30 Industrials, so a rise in the Dow to 6,000 would equate a parallel rise in S&Ps to about 706.00.

The Dow's weekly Bollinger Band width is also rising off nearly two-year lows and cleared Gabriel's signal line in early September. He said that suggested a market "on the verge of a trending resolution" after a six-month trading range.
But not all analysts expect a straight shot higher.
"I still think we're vulnerable to a little swing back to work off the overbought condition," said Greg Nie, senior vice president, technical research, EVEREN Securities.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see a little backing and filling going into the (jobs) number on Friday," Nie added.
He said New York Stock Exchange volume during the recent swing higher was not high enough to keep momentum going.
"I think at this stage of the game it's going to require a continuation of the really robust volume to counteract the overbought condition," he said.

But Nie also noted that December S&P 500s recently have respected trendline support at the 685.00 level on pullbacks and that any correction likely would halt in the low-690 to upper-680 area. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
